gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.

gaps.sentence: The critics ___ praise on the young violinist.
gaps.explanation: 'Heap praise on' = give a great deal of praise.

gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: It was three in the morning, but I was wide ___.
gaps.explanation: wide awake means completely awake; it is the fixed collocation with 'wide'.

gaps.sentence: The scientists are ___ research into new forms of energy.
gaps.explanation: do research (into something) is the collocation; 'make research' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Even after she moved abroad, we ___ in touch by email.
gaps.explanation: keep in touch means to maintain contact with someone.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.
